title: Tech Note: Selecting the Proper Transport Layer on the Macintosh Version of 4D Server
author: Christopher Chapman

historical_commentary.text: This note explains why a Macintosh running 4D Server must select the Ethernet (native packet format) transport layer rather than EtherTalk (AppleTalk-encapsulated) when Windows 4D Clients need to connect, since most PCs of the era lacked AppleTalk stack support; AppleTalk networking itself was discontinued by Apple in the 2000s, and the entire transport-layer-selection concern is obsolete now that all platforms use standard TCP/IP.
related_updates: AppleTalk networking protocol was discontinued by Apple in the 2000s (Mac OS X eventually dropped AppleTalk support entirely)
All modern 4D Server/Client connections use standard TCP/IP exclusively; there is no EtherTalk-vs-Ethernet transport layer choice to make anymore
MacTCP and MacIPX control panels are classic Mac OS artifacts with no equivalent in any current operating system
